correctness.rationale: A local private-neighbor iff criterion gives a complete finite subset scan; independent incremental hypergraph minimal transversals give identical sorted families for every order 1 through 17. Exact integer Walsh transforms verify the full transition table, the 15 zero pairs, 19516 zero characters at 17, least positive multiplier magnitude 2, and second-transform absolute sum 3341768. Translation averaging proves the projection lower bound over all real/complex projections. All calculations were rerun from the embedded executable; no infinite extrapolation is made.

evidence: The exact complete-bipartite signed minimal-domination result covers complete bipartite graphs, not the seventeen-vertex path.
Maximal independent sets of a path are always minimal dominating but at order 17 form only 114 of the 268 minimal dominating sets; this does not determine the larger sum.
Chordal-graph enumeration covers path membership but does not supply signed weighted counts.

Kanté et al. (2013) furnish a general minimal-dominating-set counting/enumeration method for interval graphs, which includes every path, but the inspected results do not derive the binary signed transform.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Inclusion of the underlying class into a broader graph-algorithm theorem is not inclusion of the spectral conclusion. The strictly smaller maximal-independent-set codebook has a distinct Walsh kernel, and the complete-bipartite results are neither graph minors nor spectral extensions furnishing the target values.

value.rationale: The seventeen-vertex path is the first natural boundary where every first-order signed marginal is nonzero yet Fourier inversion is singular, detected for the first time by 15 second-order interactions. The exact nullity and globally sharp endpoint projection constant quantify a concrete recovery obstruction, rather than merely recomputing an unsigned count. This finite obstruction is a useful small benchmark for signed transversal/multivariate domination methods; no grander claim is made.
